elements.label: Figure A.2.1.1
elements.description: Stacked bar chart, LMIC ($3.20/day 2011PPP). Y-axis: 'Decomposed change in poverty rate (p.p)', range -35 to 15 with gridlines every 5. X-axis categories: National; Midlands & Northern Mountains; Red River Delta; Northern & Coastal Center; Central Highlands; Southeast; Mekong Delta; Ethnic minority; Kinh majority. Legend: Adult share (teal), Employed share (orange), Farm income (grey), Labor income (p.e) (yellow), Non-farm income (blue), Non-labor income (green), Propensity score (purple). No values are printed. Approximate readings, National: Farm income ~+3, Propensity score ~+2, Labor income (p.e) ~-15, Non-farm income ~-1, Adult share ~-2, Non-labor income ~-3, total ~-19. Midlands & Northern Mountains: Propensity ~+2, Farm ~+5, Labor income ~-22, Non-farm ~-2, Non-labor ~-3, Propensity (negative) ~-3, total ~-28. Red River Delta: Propensity ~+4, Farm ~+4, Employed ~+2, Adult ~+2, Labor income ~-17, Non-labor ~-3, total ~-19. Kinh majority: Adult ~-2, Labor income ~-30, Non-labor ~-2, Propensity ~-2, Farm ~+3. Pattern: labor income (p.e) is the largest negative contributor in nearly every region, while propensity score and farm income are the main positive offsets, and Kinh majority shows the largest reduction.

elements.label: Figure A.2.1.2
elements.description: Stacked bar chart, National, LMIC ($3.20/day 2011PPP). Y-axis: 'Decomposed change in poverty rate (p.p)', range -20 to 15. X-axis: 2010–2020 and 2014–2020. Legend: Adult share (teal), Employed share (orange), Farm income (grey), Labor income (Ag, p.e) (yellow), Labor income (Manu, p.e.) (light blue), Labor income (Serv, p.e) (green), Non-farm income (purple), Propensity score (dark red). No values printed. Approximate readings, 2010–2020: Propensity score ~+4.5, Farm income ~+4.5, Employed share ~+0.5, Labor income (Ag) ~+0.5, Labor income (Manu) ~-8.5, Labor income (Serv) ~-5, Non-farm income ~-2.3; total ~-16 to net positive ~+10 top. 2014–2020: Propensity score ~+3, Farm income ~+2, Employed share ~+0.5, Adult share ~+0.5, Labor income (Manu) ~-7.3, Labor income (Serv) ~-3.5, Non-farm income ~-1.8. Pattern: manufacturing and service labor income drive the decline in poverty in both periods, while the propensity score and farm income push poverty up, with a smaller contribution in the 2014–2020 period.

elements.label: Figure A.2.1.3
elements.description: Stacked bar chart of household income decomposition, 2010–2020. Y-axis: 'Decomposed changed in Gini index (p.p)', range -0.15 to 0.09 with gridlines at 0.03 intervals. X-axis categories: National; Midlands & Northern Mountains; Red River Delta; Northern & Coastal Center; Central Highlands; Southeast; Mekong Delta; Ethnic minority; Kinh majority. Legend: Adult share (teal), Employed share (orange), Labor income (p.e) (grey), Farm income (yellow), Non-farm income (blue), Non-labor income (green). No values printed. Approximate readings, National: Farm ~+0.025, Adult ~-0.02, Labor income ~-0.04, Non-farm ~-0.02, Employed ~+0.005. Midlands & Northern Mountains: Farm ~+0.045, Adult ~-0.01, Non-labor ~-0.01. Red River Delta: Farm ~+0.035, Labor income ~-0.025, Non-farm ~-0.02, Non-labor ~-0.02. Central Highlands: Farm ~+0.015, Employed ~+0.02, Labor income ~+0.03, Adult ~-0.02, Non-labor ~-0.01. Southeast: Labor income ~-0.07, Farm ~-0.03, Non-labor ~-0.02, Employed ~+0.01. Kinh majority: Farm ~+0.03, Adult ~-0.02, Non-labor ~-0.01. Pattern: farm income and labor income shift the Gini index in opposite directions across regions, with the Southeast showing the largest labor income effect.
